chunks: And it has been narrated from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام that he said:

"On the twenty-fifth of Dhī al-Qaʿdah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the Kaʿbah, the Sacred House. So whoever fasts on that day, it is an expiation for seventy years. And it is the first day on which mercy was sent down from the heaven upon Ādam عليه السلام."

key_terms.آدَمَ: Ādam عليه السلام, upon whom that mercy was sent down.
key_terms.الرَّحْمَةُ: Divine mercy that was sent down from the heaven.
key_terms.الْبَيْتَ الْحَرَامَ: The Sacred House, referring to the sanctified sanctuary in Makkah.
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: The Kaʿbah, identified here as the Sacred House sent down by Allah.
key_terms.ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ: The month of Dhī al-Qaʿdah in which this virtuous day occurs.
key_terms.صَامَ: Observed sawm, referring to fasting on this specific day.
key_terms.كَفَّارَةَ: Expiation or atonement granted for fasting on that day.

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of fasting on the twenty-fifth of Dhī al-Qaʿdah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the special merit of the twenty-fifth of Dhī al-Qaʿdah, linking it to the sending down of the Kaʿbah and the descent of divine mercy upon Ādam عليه السلام. It emphasizes the virtue of sawm on that day, stating that it serves as expiation for seventy years.
